title: Functions, Closures & Variadic
intro: Go functions are first-class values — you can assign them to variables, pass them as arguments, and return them from other functions. This module covers Go's function syntax (named functions vs anonymous function literals), multiple return values (the Go idiom of returning a result and an error together — (value, error)), named return values and why they are sometimes useful and sometimes confusing, closures in Go (how a function literal captures variables from its enclosing scope, the loop variable capture gotcha that catches everyone once), variadic functions (the ...T syntax, how to spread a slice into a variadic call), defer (how deferred calls execute LIFO at function return, the argument evaluation timing — a common interview trick question), and panic/recover as the last-resort mechanism for genuinely unrecoverable errors. These fundamentals underpin every pattern in more advanced Go code.
